transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [name], nice to meet you. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Nice to meet you. I guess I'm here because... well, ever since I moved into this busted-up room I'm renting, things have just been bad. I'm snapping at people all the time. I end up staying up half the night trying to fix leaks or get the heat working, and then I'm just dragging myself into work late. I work construction, and lately I've been messing up stuff on the site that I normally handle with no problem. It's just getting to be a lot to deal with.
About how long ago did you move into this room, and how soon after that did you start noticing these changes in your mood and behavior?

Well, I was doing pretty normal before I moved into that room. I guess all this started within the first couple weeks of being there... you know, right after I found the water damage and realized the heat was messed up.
Besides feeling irritable, have you noticed yourself feeling more sad, anxious, or worried since all this started?

Not really. I mean, I don't feel sad or anything like that. And I wouldn't say I'm worried or anxious... just, you know, stressed out. It's really just the frustration of it all. Mostly I'm just mad that I'm stuck dealing with this crap every day and being so tired, but no, I haven't really noticed feeling down or panicky.
Have you noticed this irritability or exhaustion causing problems in your relationships with family or friends, or affecting other parts of your daily life outside of work?

Well, mostly it's just hitting me at work. Like I said, I've been messing up on the site, and my foreman actually pulled me aside. He told me I could lose my shot at moving up to crew lead if I keep slipping like this. And honestly, I've already messed up some work paperwork and had scheduling problems because my head's just not in it with all this going on. As for friends or family... I don't know, I guess I just haven't had the energy to really see anybody anyway.
Since you moved in a couple weeks ago, would you say you've been feeling this irritable and on-edge nearly every day, or does it come and go depending on what's happening with the room?

Well, actually, it's been a bit longer than a couple weeks. It's been going on for about a month now. It started up shortly after I moved into that Bridgeport room. And yeah... it's pretty much every single day. It doesn't really come and go because, I mean, I have to go back to that room every night, so I'm just always on edge about it.
Have you had any actual outbursts—like yelling at coworkers, getting into arguments, or doing anything impulsive or reckless—because of how irritable and on edge you've been feeling?

No, nothing like that. I haven't yelled at anyone or gotten into any fights. I keep it to myself, mostly. I mean, I'm definitely annoyed and short with people in my head, but I don't blow up at work or do anything crazy. It's just... a constant frustration, you know? But I'm not acting out or anything.
Would you say you find yourself constantly preoccupied or worrying about the room situation even when you're not there—like at work or trying to relax—more than you'd expect for a housing problem?

I don't really think so. I mean... I'm not sitting at work just obsessing over the room all day. I'm trying to focus on my job. It's more that I'm just exhausted and annoyed from the whole situation. Like, it sucks knowing I have to go back there when my shift is done, but I wouldn't say I'm constantly worrying about it or anything like that when I'm not there.

Compared to how you think most people would react to dealing with a bad living situation like this, would you say your stress, irritability, and trouble functioning at work feel a lot more intense or harder to manage than what you'd expect, or does it feel like a fairly normal reaction to the hassle?

I mean... I don't really know how other people would handle it, to be honest. It's a huge hassle, and it's definitely messing with my sleep and making work harder. But... I don't know if it's more intense than what anyone else would feel. It just feels like a normal reaction to being stuck in a really crappy situation. I think anyone would be this stressed out and tired if they were dealing with it.
Has your foreman given you any formal warnings or disciplinary action because of these work mistakes, or is it just a verbal heads-up so far?

It hasn't been a formal write-up yet, but he did pull me aside. He told me I could lose my shot at moving up to crew lead if I keep slipping up like this. And I've already had some issues with my paperwork and scheduling lately because my head's just not in it. So it's definitely starting to cause some real problems for me there.

Do you feel like your sleep problems, irritability, and mistakes at work are actually interfering with your ability to function—like potentially costing you your job or relationships—beyond just being an unpleasant hassle?

Yeah, I mean... like I was just saying, it's definitely getting past just being a hassle. It's actually messing with my job. My foreman told me I could lose my shot at moving up to crew lead if I keep slipping up. And with the paperwork and scheduling problems I've already been having because of all this... yeah, it's definitely interfering with my work, for sure.
